# Stork of Attribution (`stork-of-attribution`)

Reconciles a value-based contract's attribution roster with your visits: active patients the payer left out, patients dropped since last month, patients attributed to a provider who never saw them, attributed patients you have not seen, and new adds. Patient names, member IDs and birth dates are masked before results reach the model.

**Stork never sends attribution disputes to a payer. Stork never contacts patients.**

Kestrel ver 1 · Care management and value-based care · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`kestrel-core`](../kestrel-core)

```bash
npx -y stork-of-attribution demo
npx -y stork-of-attribution mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: a made-up practice, payer ("Bluepeak Advantage"), members and providers. Any likeness to real people is chance. NPIs are made up with valid check digits.

- [`roster-2026-11.csv`](fixtures/roster-2026-11.csv), [`roster-2026-10.csv`](fixtures/roster-2026-10.csv) and [`visits.csv`](fixtures/visits.csv). Planted:
  - Tara Wu: seen twice in 2026 under Bluepeak, on neither roster (left out).
  - Ruth Banks: on October's roster, gone in November, seen in September (dropped while active).
  - Quinn Mayer: attributed to Dr. Otto, seen three times by Dr. Lin and never by Dr. Otto.
  - Paulo Grant: attributed but never seen. Uma Field: last seen March 2024, outside the 24-month lookback.
  - Sven Holt: new on November's roster.
  - Vic Romero is a Cedar Mutual patient and is ignored.
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): 24-month lookback, Bluepeak visits only, and an example 40 a month per member. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

## A demo run

`npx -y stork-of-attribution demo` runs the agent on the fictional files in [`fixtures/`](fixtures) in a temporary folder. Captured output:

```text

▶ Reconcile the November roster with visits
  status: executed  decision: allow
  5 attributed (5 last month), 5 active patient(s) with this payer. 80 a month at risk. 6 finding(s): left_out 1, dropped 1, wrong_provider 1, not_seen 2, added 1.
    left_out           40  Active patient (2 visit(s), last 2026-07-29) with this payer is not on the attribution roster.
    dropped            40  On last month's roster but not this month's; still seen here (last visit 2026-09-22).
    wrong_provider      0  Attributed to Sam Otto DO but seen 3 time(s) by Rhea Lin MD and never by the attributed provider.
    not_seen            0  Attributed to you; last visit 2024-03-05, outside the lookback.
    not_seen            0  Attributed to you but never seen here.
    added               0  New on this month's roster.

▶ Write the reconciliation
  status: executed  decision: allow
  Attribution reconciliation written: 5 attributed (5 last month), 5 active patient(s) with this payer. 80 a month at risk. 6 finding(s): left_out 1, dropped 1, wrong_provider 1, not_seen 2, added 1. Files: kestrel-out/stork/stork-attribution.csv, kestrel-out/stork/stork-attribution.html.

▶ Agent tries to send a dispute to the payer
  status: blocked  decision: block
  reason: Stork never sends attribution disputes to a payer.
```

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `stork_check` | List patients left out, dropped, attributed to the wrong provider, not seen and newly added. | runs |
| `stork_write_report` | Write stork-attribution.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and stork-attribution.html into out_dir (default kestrel-out/stork). | runs |
| `stork_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `stork_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `stork_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `stork_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `roster_dispute_submit` | Stork never sends attribution disputes to a payer. | refused |
| `patient_outreach_send` | Stork never contacts patients. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `stork_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `roster` (required) | This month's attribution roster from the payer under --root: member ID, name, date of birth, attributed provider or NPI |
| `prior` | Optional: last month's roster, to list adds and drops |
| `visits` (required) | Your visit list: patient, member ID, name, date of birth, date, provider, NPI, payer |
| `settings` | Optional settings JSON: lookback_months, payer_words, pmpm |
| `as_of` | Date to measure deadlines and ages from (YYYY-MM-DD); default today |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx stork-of-attribution inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Attribution roster (`roster`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `member_id` | text (masked) | Member ID, Member #, Subscriber ID, Insurance ID, MBI, Beneficiary ID, Policy # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `dob` | date (masked) | DOB, Date of Birth, Birth Date, Birthdate |
| `provider` | text | Attributed Provider, PCP, Provider, Assigned Provider, PCP Name |
| `npi` | text | PCP NPI, Attributed NPI, NPI, Provider NPI |

### Last month's roster (`prior`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `member_id` | text (masked) | Member ID, Member #, Subscriber ID, Insurance ID, MBI, Beneficiary ID, Policy # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `dob` | date (masked) | DOB, Date of Birth, Birth Date, Birthdate |
| `provider` | text | Attributed Provider, PCP, Provider, Assigned Provider, PCP Name |
| `npi` | text | PCP NPI, Attributed NPI, NPI, Provider NPI |

### Visits (`visits`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `patient_id` | text (masked) | Patient ID, Patient #, Patient Number, MRN, Medical Record Number, Chart #, Chart Number, Account # |
| `member_id` | text (masked) | Member ID, Member #, Subscriber ID, Insurance ID, MBI, Beneficiary ID, Policy # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `dob` | date (masked) | DOB, Date of Birth, Birth Date, Birthdate |
| `date` (required) | date | Date of Service, DOS, Service Date, Visit Date, Date, From DOS, Session Date, Appointment Date |
| `provider` | text | Provider, Rendering Provider, Rendering, Clinician, Therapist, Physician, Doctor, Practitioner |
| `npi` | text | NPI, Provider NPI, Rendering NPI, Individual NPI |
| `payer` | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Insurance, Insurance Name, Plan, Plan Name, Payor |

## Settings file (`stork_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `lookback_months` | Months of visits that make a patient active; default 24 (contracts vary) |
| `payer_words` | Words in the visit payer column that mean this contract's payer |
| `pmpm` | Monthly payment per attributed member, to price patients left out or dropped |

## Memory

`stork_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `stork_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `kestrel-core` and `remedy-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "stork-of-attribution": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "stork-of-attribution",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add stork-of-attribution -- npx -y stork-of-attribution mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
stork-of-attribution tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
stork-of-attribution sources               # the columns each input is read from
stork-of-attribution inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
stork-of-attribution call stork_check '{"roster":"<roster>","visits":"<visits>"}'
stork-of-attribution eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
stork-of-attribution demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
